Barium hexaferrite (BaFe12O19) has a hexagonal crystal structure with high coercivity (~6700 Oe) and high magnetization (~78 emu/g).
The sol-gel auto combustion method produces homogeneous barium hexaferrite nanoparticles.
Starting materials included ferric nitrate nonahydrate, barium nitrate, and nitric acid.
The molar ratio of Fe to Ba was fixed at 11:1 in the precursor solution.
pH was adjusted to 7.5, 9, and 11 using ammonia during synthesis.
Stirring times tested were 1, 2, and 3 hours.
The sol-gel auto combustion reaction was conducted at 100°C for 30 minutes to form solid material.
Sintering was performed at 950°C for 2.5 hours to crystallize barium hexaferrite.
SEM showed particle morphology changed from agglomerated (pH 7.5) to porous (pH 9) to flake-like (pH 11).
XRD confirmed formation of BaFe12O19 and Fe2O3 phases, with optimal BaFe12O19 formation at pH 7.5 and 2 hours stirring.
The smallest crystalline size was 414.409 nm at pH 7.5 and 2 hours stirring.
The largest crystalline size was 994.778 nm at pH 11 and 3 hours stirring.
Magnetic coercivity peaked at 0.6 Tesla for pH 7.5 and 2 hours stirring.
Magnetic saturation reached 55.54 emu/g at pH 7.5 and 1 hour stirring.
Increasing pH above 7.5 decreased magnetic coercivity.
Longer stirring time improved homogeneity and reduced particle size but could reduce magnetic saturation.
Magnetic remanence and coercivity depend strongly on particle size and microstructure.
The magnetic properties achieved meet the requirements for radar absorber material applications.
The Debye-Scherrer equation was used to calculate crystalline size from XRD data.
The sol-gel auto combustion method offers advantages such as simple reagents, short processing time, and good chemical homogeneity.
